correctness.rationale: For each alternating cycle, the first moved original edge must be replaced with a temporary edge from an exposed vertex outside the cycle; this is a non-target insertion. Adding necessary target-edge insertions gives the exact lower bound. The path-following and temporary-hole cycle algorithm meets it. The exponential labeled-block decomposition counts each state exactly once; the diameter and antipodal counts follow from maximizing the cycle count subject to each nontrivial cycle using at least two matching edges. Two dissimilar executable scripts independently reproduce all distance polynomials for 1<=m<=5, one from BFS flip edges and one from cycle decompositions plus species recurrence. These finite computations corroborate, not prove, the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The full labeled distance polynomial and exact antipodal counts for 1-flips of almost-perfect matchings in every odd complete graph are not supplied by the inspected results. The 2018 matching-distance paper treats general graph complexity; Jennings (2013 preprint) and Cioabă–Royle–Tan study 2-edge flips on even-order perfect matchings; Aichholzer et al. introduce/analyze almost-perfect 1-flips, and Brenner et al. prove Hamilton-connectedness of this same graph. These statements do not imply the displayed distance distribution. A close literature gap remains between a known flip model and unknown full metric census; priority risk persists for unindexed sources.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently named all-pairs distance enumerations may exist.
General reconfiguration methods may provide simpler alternative proofs; shared lower-bound insight in Aichholzer et al. is credited.

value.rationale: The exact all-distance spectrum of a natural vertex-transitive reconfiguration graph gives more than Hamiltonicity or a shortest-path upper bound. The species polynomial explicitly counts every geodesic shell for arbitrary odd complete graphs, determines the sharp diameter and counts all antipodes in closed form, providing nontrivial infinite-family structural enumeration. The invariant has direct meaning as the distribution of optimum numbers of local edits between feasible maximum matchings; the calculation is not an isolated arbitrary slice.
